title: A Dirac-Frenkel-Onsager principle: Instantaneous residual minimization with gauge momentum for nonlinear parametrizations of PDE solutions
claim: Standard instantaneous-residual dynamics get stuck after a rank-collapse singularity and incur large error, while ours escapes and tracks truth.
layout: 5 stacked panels sharing time axis: three heatmaps, then two line plots
description: Five vertically stacked panels share a time axis from 0 to 4. The top three are viridis heatmaps of a wave solution over a spatial domain: ground truth, Dirac-Frenkel labeled 'stuck after collapse', and the proposed Dirac-Frenkel-Onsager (ours). A black vertical line at t=2 marks the wave collision. In the truth and in ours, the yellow band widens and then fades after t=2. In the Dirac-Frenkel panel the band stays a thin bright stripe, locked in place. Below are two log-scale line plots, condition number and L2 error, for DF (blue) and DFO (orange). Both spike at t=2. After the spike, DF stays near 1e12 condition number and its error jumps to about 1e-2. DFO recovers to a low condition number and a small error. The eye goes first to the heatmap contrast.
caption: At wave collision (t = 2), the tangent space collapses and so Dirac-Frenkel (even with minimal-norm regularization) yields a parameter velocity that keeps the waves locked together. In contrast, the proposed Dirac-Frenkel-Onsager principle keeps injecting momentum in the nullspace direction at rank loss and so the dynamics can escape the collapse.
abstract: Dirac-Frenkel instantaneous residual minimization evolves nonlinear parametrizations of PDE solutions in time, but ill-conditioning can render the parameter dynamics non-unique. We interpret this non-uniqueness as a gauge freedom: nullspace directions that leave the time derivative unchanged can be used to select better-conditioned parameter velocities. Building on Onsager's minimum-dissipation principle, we introduce a history variable -- interpretable as momentum -- and inject it only along the nullspace directions. The resulting Dirac-Frenkel-Onsager dynamics preserve instantaneous residual minimization, in contrast to standard regularization that can introduce bias, while promoting temporally smooth parameter evolutions. Examples demonstrate that the approach leads to increased robustness in singular and near-singular regimes.
